name: Weekly competitor content digest from RSS feeds

nodes.name: Every Monday at 8am
nodes.notes:
Runs every Monday at 8AM automatically.

Change the schedule if needed:
- Every Friday: 0 8 * * 5
- Twice a week: 0 8 * * 1,4
- Every day: 0 8 * * *

No credentials needed.

nodes.name: Set config
nodes.notes:
REPLACE THESE VALUES:

1. competitor1RssUrl (pre-filled with Ahrefs as example)
   Replace with your actual competitor's RSS feed
   How to find it: try yourcompetitor.com/feed or yourcompetitor.com/rss
   For example: https://backlinko.com/feed

2. competitor2RssUrl (pre-filled with Search Engine Journal)
   Replace with your second competitor

3. competitor3Name and competitor3RssUrl
   Optional — leave URL blank to skip this competitor

4. yourNiche
   Your industry — GPT uses this to find relevant content gaps
   Example: SEO for law firms, e-commerce marketing, SaaS content marketing

5. recipientEmail
   Who receives the Monday morning digest
   Example: you@example.com

6. senderName
   Your name for the email sign-off

7. sheetId
   Open your Google Sheet in browser
   URL: docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1ABC123/edit
   Copy the part between /d/ and /edit
   Create a tab called: Competitor Content
   Row 1 headers:
   Week | Competitor | Post 1 Title | Post 2 Title | Post 3 Title | Post 4 Title | Post 5 Title | Post Count | Logged At

nodes.name: Build the competitor list
nodes.notes:
Creates one item per competitor from the config.
Filters out competitors with blank URLs.
Adds isLastCompetitor = true on the final competitor.
This flag is used later to trigger the Gmail digest after all are processed.
No changes needed.

nodes.name: Fetch the RSS feed
nodes.notes:
Fetches the RSS XML from the competitor's blog feed.

timeout: 15 seconds
onError: continueRegularOutput — if a feed fails, the workflow continues
and the Parse node returns empty posts with an error note

If a feed fails consistently:
- Check the RSS URL is correct
- Some sites block bot requests — try adding a User-Agent header

No credentials needed — RSS feeds are public.

nodes.name: Read the posts from the feed
nodes.notes:
Parses the RSS XML and extracts the 5 most recent post titles.

Handles both RSS 2.0 (item tags) and Atom (entry tags) formats.
Handles both CDATA and plain text title formats.
If the feed fails or returns no posts, outputs empty posts gracefully
so the workflow can continue without breaking.

No changes needed.

nodes.name: Log the posts
nodes.notes:
Logs this competitor's posts to Google Sheets permanently.

How to connect:
1. Go to console.cloud.google.com and enable Google Sheets API
2. In n8n: Settings → Credentials → Add New → Google Sheets OAuth2
3. Authenticate and connect to this node

Sheet tab: Competitor Content
Row 1 headers:
Week | Competitor | Post 1 Title | Post 2 Title | Post 3 Title | Post 4 Title | Post 5 Title | Post Count | Logged At

Every Monday adds rows for all competitors.
Filter by Week to see any past week's data.
Filter by Competitor to track one source over time.

nodes.name: Last competitor?
nodes.notes:
Checks if all competitors have been processed.

TRUE — last competitor logged — now build and send the digest
FALSE — more competitors still being processed — continue silently

Reads isLastCompetitor from Build Competitors List directly.
All previous competitors' posts are already in Google Sheets by the time this fires.
No changes needed.

nodes.name: Read this week's posts
nodes.notes:
Reads only this week's rows from the Competitor Content sheet.

Connect the same Google Sheets credential here.

Filter: Week column = current week label
This returns all competitors' posts that were logged in this run.
These rows are then sent to GPT for analysis.

nodes.name: Prepare the data for GPT
nodes.notes:
Reads all this week's rows from Google Sheets.
Builds a clean structured text showing what each competitor published.
This becomes the input for GPT analysis.
No changes needed.

nodes.name: Write the digest
nodes.notes:
GPT analyzes all competitor posts from this week and returns 5 structured fields:

1. weekSummary — 2 to 3 sentences on what the competitive landscape looks like
2. competitorHighlights — top post and strategy angle per competitor
3. trendingTopics — 3 topics appearing across multiple competitors
4. contentGaps — 3 specific content ideas no competitor covered
5. urgentOpportunity — the one piece to publish this week

The Digest Output Parser below ensures clean JSON every time.
Output is in $json.output

parameters.text:
=You are a competitive content analyst for a {{ $json.yourNiche }} business.

Here are the blog posts published this week by our competitors:

{{ $json.competitorData }}

Week: {{ $json.weekLabel }}

Analyze this competitor content and return ONLY a valid JSON object. No extra text. No markdown. No backticks.

Required fields:

weekSummary
2 to 3 sentences summarizing the overall competitive content landscape this week. What themes are emerging across these competitors? Keep it specific to the actual posts listed.

competitorHighlights
Array of objects — one per competitor that published content. Each object must have exactly 3 fields:
name: the competitor name
topPost: the most interesting or strategically important post title from their list
angle: one sentence describing what content angle or strategy this competitor is focusing on

trendingTopics
Array of exactly 3 strings. Topics or themes that appeared across more than one competitor this week. These indicate what the market is prioritizing right now.

contentGaps
Array of exactly 3 strings. Valuable topics for a {{ $json.yourNiche }} audience that NONE of the competitors covered this week. Each gap should be a specific content idea, not a broad category.

urgentOpportunity
One string. The single most important content piece to publish this week to get ahead of competitors or fill a high-value gap. Name the exact topic or proposed article title.

nodes.name: Chat model
nodes.notes:
Connect your OpenAI API credential here.

1. Go to platform.openai.com/api-keys

3. In n8n: Settings → Credentials → Add New → OpenAI API

nodes.name: Output Parser - Digest sections
nodes.notes:
Schema: 5 required fields for the competitive digest.
Ensures GPT always returns clean consistent data.
No changes needed.

nodes.name: Build the email
nodes.notes:
Reads GPT output from $json.output.
Reads config from Format Data for GPT node.

Builds one plain text email with 5 sections:
1. Week in review — overall landscape summary
2. Competitor highlights — top post and angle per competitor
3. Trending topics — what the market is talking about
4. Content gaps — what no competitor covered (your opportunity)
5. Urgent content opportunity — the one piece to publish now

No changes needed.

nodes.name: Send the digest
nodes.notes:
Sends the weekly competitive content digest.

How to connect:
1. Go to console.cloud.google.com and enable Gmail API
2. In n8n: Settings → Credentials → Add New → Gmail OAuth2
3. Authenticate and connect to this node

Email arrives every Monday morning with:
- What each competitor published this week
- Which topics are trending across competitors
- Content gaps your competitors missed
- One urgent content opportunity to act on

parameters.content:
## 1. Settings
One config node holds up to three competitors, your niche, your email and your sheet. A Code node turns them into one item each and skips any with a blank feed URL.

## 2. Collect this week's posts
Each feed is fetched and parsed into titles, links and dates. A feed that fails does not stop the run. Every competitor's posts are appended to your sheet.

## 3. Wait for all of them
The digest is built only after the last competitor has been logged. Earlier competitors pass through silently.

## 4. Write and send the digest
This week's rows are read back, GPT finds trending topics, content gaps and urgent opportunities, and the result is formatted into one email.

# Weekly competitor content digest from RSS feeds

Every Monday this reads the blog feeds of up to three competitors, logs what they published to a Google Sheet, and has GPT turn the week's output into a short intelligence brief: what themes they are pushing, where the gaps are, and what you should write next. Arrives as one email, no dashboard to check.

### How it works
1. A Monday schedule fires and one config node holds your competitors, your niche, your email and your sheet.
2. A Code node builds one item per competitor and skips any with a blank feed URL.
3. Each feed is fetched with a fifteen second timeout. A feed that fails is recorded as empty rather than stopping the run.
4. The XML is parsed into post titles, links and dates, and each competitor's week is appended to your sheet as a permanent content library.
5. Once the last competitor is logged, this week's rows are read back and formatted for analysis.
6. GPT writes the digest: trending topics, content gaps you could own, and the most urgent opportunity.
7. Those sections are built into one email and sent to you.

### Setup
1. Add your OpenAI API key and connect your Google Sheets and Gmail accounts.
2. Open Set config and fill in each competitor name and RSS URL, your niche, email, name and sheet ID. Leave a URL blank to track fewer than three.
3. Create a tab called Competitor Content with headers for Week, Competitor, five post titles, Post Count and Logged At.
4. Most blogs expose a feed at /feed, /rss or /feed.xml.

### Customization
Change the schedule for a daily brief, or edit the agent prompt to focus on formats and keywords instead of themes.
